Brønderslev-Dronninglund is a Danish municipality evaluated in the 2022–2023 Annual Report from the Atrial Fibrillation Database in Denmark (AFDK), published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) [^src1][^src2]. The report assesses the quality of care for patients with atrial fibrillation, with a specific focus on anticoagulation treatment and safety monitoring across all 98 Danish municipalities [^src1][^src2].

Brønderslev-Dronninglund is particularly notable for its performance on Indicator 4b, which measures compliance with safety practices regarding the use of Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) [^src1]. The municipality achieved a compliance rate of 97.7% (721 out of 738 patients), a result that not only met the required standard (marked as "Yes") but also stood as the highest recorded proportion among all municipalities in the report [^src1]. Furthermore, it recorded a 95.8% rate (722 out of 754) for the associated metric within the same indicator category [^src1].

The municipality is also tracked under other clinical quality indicators, such as Indicator 1 (early initiation of anticoagulation treatment) and Indicator 5 (prevention of ischemic stroke via anticoagulation treatment) [^src2]. For these specific metrics, Brønderslev-Dronninglund reported much lower absolute numbers, registering a 0.7% rate (7 out of 956) for one measure and a 0.6% rate (6 out of 985) for another, both of which were marked as meeting the standard ("Yes") [^src2]. These detailed municipal breakdowns highlight the decentralized approach to quality development and benchmarking within the Danish healthcare system [^src1][^src2].
